newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of August 4, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Netscape Communications Corp is returning to its roots and it is working on a plan to separate Navigator 4.x from its Communicator client suite and gave back to users what they once had - a thin browser client, PC Week reported August 4.

International Business Machines Corp will provide by the end of next year a wide-ranging family of directory offerings that attempt to span the varied needs of enterprise customers, PC Week reported August 4.

COMPUTERWORLD - In a few years, millions may reach for their Visa card instead of change for the tollbooth or a company security card, as credit card giant Visa International plans to begin replacing the magnetic strips on its cards with Java-based computer chips, Computerworld reported Aug. 4.

Users and corporate developers last week expressed a mix of reactions - from alarm to knowing shrugs - in recognition that cross-platform Java may be compromised if Microsoft Corp persists in its refusal to support Sun Microsystems Inc Java Foundation Classes, Computerworld reported.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - International Business Machines Corp, Sun Microsystems Inc and Corel may give away network computers to spur sales of services, applications and servers, Computer Reseller News reported Aug. 4.
Hewlett-Packard Co and Compaq Computer Corp are nearing the starting game of a horse race to best IBM's PC Co in channel assembly, CRN reported Aug. 4.

INFOWORLD - Despite turbulence in its management structure, Informix Corp is embarking on a grand scheme to position its Universal Server relational database as so-called "middleware" software tool for applications based on three-tier architectures, Infoworld reported August 4.

At MacWorld Expo this week in Boston, Apple Computer Inc and major Mac clone vendors Power Computing and Motorola Inc will face off with hardware offerings that differ in processors and platform standards, InfoWorld reported Aug. 4.

INFORMATION WEEK - International Business Machines Corp is unveiling an upgrade of its AS/400 minicomputer line on Aug. 18 called the AS/400e as the computer giant refocuses the line as a secure server for electronic commerce, Information Week reported Aug. 4.
Push technology is gaining momentum in the corporate enterprise for more productive applications - to boost sales, broad marketing and tweak internal processes, Information Week reported Aug. 4.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - Spot market prices for 16-bit Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) chips have fallen to the lowest levels in a year, falling more than 20 percent since May, and triggering production cutback in South Korea and Japan, Electronic Buyers News reported Aug. 4.

Analysts are still unsure how soon National Semiconductor Corp can integrate newly-acquired Cyrix Corp's processor core with its own technology, how quickly it can market it and what response it can expect from rivals Intel Corp and Advanced Micro Devices Inc, Electronic Buyers News reported Aug. 4.
EE TIMES - An Intel Corp unit has completed an
unannounced plan for its Pentium II chip which includeds new module and chip-level versions of the processor geared to the needs of embedded systems designers, EE Times reported Aug. 4.

MACWEEK - The rumors surrounding Steve Jobs' possible return to the top spot at Apple Computer Inc reached a crescendo last week, with most of the reports claiming he would be named CEO or chairman of the board at this week's MacWorld Expo in Boston, MacWeek reported Aug. 4.

Speculation also swirled around the Mac camp about candidates for the vacant seats on the Apple board with the list including a bevvy of computer-industry heavyweights. Larry Ellison, CEO of Oracle Corp, said he would be join Apple's board in a deal in which he would own a share of the company, MacWeek reported Aug. 4.
On Friday, sources also said that Apple is retreating from its licensing strategy, MacWeek reported Aug. 4.
